planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost; Erjingtiao is the mild, deeply fragrant chili that anchors Sichuan chili oil and doubanjiang.

directions: Pinch off side shoots below the first fruit cluster to force strong upright growth, then let the plant branch freely afterward. Harvest pods green for a mild vegetable-like chili or let them color to a glossy deep red for drying and oil-making, since Erjingtiao's thin walls and high aromatic oil content make it dry quickly on screens or strings. Unlike many Capsicum annuum types bred mainly for heat, this cultivar is prized for fragrance and color over pungency, so expect only moderate spiciness even at full ripeness. Plants perform best with steady warmth and consistent moisture through fruit set to avoid blossom drop.
sources: Chili Pepper Madness — Growing Chili Peppers Guide

common_name: Xiao Mi La Chili Pepper (Yunnan Millet Pepper)

planting.note: Start indoors on a heat mat 8-10 weeks before last frost; this frutescens type germinates slowly and unevenly without steady warmth.

directions: Xiao Mi La ('little rice pepper') grows wild and semi-wild across southern Yunnan as a short-lived perennial shrub, and garden plants reward the same treatment as other frutescens types: warm, humid conditions and tolerance of poor, lean soil. The pencil-eraser-sized pods ripen from green to a glossy orange-red and carry some of the sharpest heat of any widely grown Chinese chili, so a single plant's harvest goes a long way in dried form. Because the species naturally branches into a bushy, multi-stemmed shrub, give it more room than a typical annual pepper and expect continuous small flushes of fruit rather than one large harvest. In frost-free gardens it can be overwintered and will resume cropping the following year.
sources: Radical Family Farms — Xiao Mi La

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in lean, sharply drained, slightly acidic soil; Hanyuan huajiao from Qingxi township carries a protected geographic-indication status dating back to its use as an imperial tribute pepper.

directions: This regional selection of Sichuan pepper is harvested from the hillsides around Qingxi in Hanyuan County, where growers consider it the most aromatic and intensely numbing of all commercial huajiao sources, with a brighter citrus-like top note than ordinary field-grown stock. The thorny, multi-stemmed shrub is dioecious, so only female plants bear the red, husk-splitting fruit clusters that are hand-picked and sun- or kiln-dried in early autumn. It tolerates poor, rocky soil and short droughts well but resents soggy winter ground, which quickly leads to root rot. Because of its mountain-valley origin, give it a sheltered site out of harsh winter wind and avoid pushing it with heavy nitrogen, which dilutes the oil content that gives the peppercorns their signature flavor.
sources: The Mala Market — Sichuan Tribute Pepper
Frontiers in Plant Science — Chemical and Genetic Characteristics of Szechuan Pepper Cultivars

planting.note: Plant grafted or seedling trees in spring beneath the dappled shade of taller companion trees in rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil; this Trinitario-type selection is traditionally grown across the Dominican Republic's cacao belt.

directions: Hispaniola cacao descends from Trinitario stock — the historic cross of Criollo and Forastero introduced to the island in the early 1600s — and today accounts for only a small share of the Dominican Republic's total cacao crop despite its reputation for a mild, low-acid cup with notes of yellow fruit. Give it an understory position with filtered light, since direct tropical sun scorches the broad leaves, and keep humidity and soil moisture consistent year-round. Pods are traditionally fermented five to seven days before drying, a longer fermentation than many origins use, which develops the variety's characteristic smooth, full-bodied flavor. Protect young trees from any temperature below the mid-50s°F, since even brief chilly spells can set back growth significantly.
sources: Felchlin — Cacao from the Dominican Republic
Missouri Botanical Garden — Theobroma cacao Plant Finder

planting.note: Start seed indoors on a heat mat 8-10 weeks before the last frost; chinense types germinate slowly and unevenly without steady bottom warmth.

directions: Jamaican Red Scotch Bonnet carries the same squat, crinkled bonnet shape as its yellow counterpart but ripens to a deep, glossy red with a slightly smokier, less citrusy edge to its fruity heat. It shares the roughly 100,000-350,000 Scoville range typical of the type, hot enough to out-pace a habanero while keeping the sweeter, tropical aroma that defines true scotch bonnets in Jamaican jerk seasoning and hot sauce. Give the plant a long warm season and even moisture, since erratic watering tends to produce smaller, thinner-walled pods. Wait for pods to fully color before picking, since green fruit lacks both the heat and the signature fruitiness the variety is grown for.
sources: Pepper Joe's — Red Scotch Bonnet Pepper
True Leaf Market — Scotch Bonnet Red

planting.note: Press seed onto the surface of moist starting mix without covering — it needs light to germinate — 6-8 weeks before last frost, then transplant once soil has warmed.

directions: Criollo is the foundational landrace behind nearly every tobacco seed line grown in Cuba's Vuelta Abajo region, prized historically for a fine-textured, reddish, highly aromatic leaf used in cigar filler and binder. Older Criollo lines are notably susceptible to blue mold and other fungal pressure, which is why modern Cuban-seed hybrids like Criollo '98 were bred in to retain the leaf quality while adding disease resistance — gardeners growing the older heirloom strain should watch humid plantings closely for early signs of mold. Transplant into fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun, and top the plant by removing the flower head once it reaches the desired leaf count to push more energy into leaf size and thickness. Leaves are traditionally primed from the bottom up as they ripen rather than harvested all at once.
sources: Terra Mater Gardens — Criollo Tobacco Seeds

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; this vigorous indeterminate vine needs a sturdy cage or stake from the time of transplanting.

directions: Cuban Black is an open-pollinated indeterminate heirloom that sets small clusters of two to five beefsteak-type fruits with mahogany-red skin shot through with dark brown highlights and distinctly ribbed green shoulders near the stem. The rich, mild flesh is lower in acid than many black or bicolor heirlooms, making it a good slicing tomato for fresh eating rather than canning. Because the vine keeps producing steadily through a long midsummer season, prune suckers periodically to keep airflow open and fruit size consistent on a trellis or cage. Pick when the shoulders fully color, since this variety can look ripe at the base while the top is still green.
sources: Tradewinds Fruit — Black Cuban Tomato Seeds
